title: Capacity planner export for Sales quoting (Dedicated tiers/shapes by region)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
description:
## Context
Sales (and Deal Desk) need a quoting-friendly view of what Dedicated shapes are currently available by region, expected lead times if not available, and the headroom assumptions by tier (Standard/Plus/Premium). Today this info lives in a mix of spreadsheets + tribal knowledge in #eng-infra and creates avoidable back-and-forth, plus over-promising risk.

This ticket is to produce a *standard export* that Sales Ops can reference when quoting Dedicated capacity.

Primary consumers:
- Sales / Solutions: quick “what can we sell in us-east vs eu-west”
- Sales Ops / Deal Desk: enforce guardrails, trigger procurement escalation when lead times exceed thresholds
- Infra/Fleet: reduce ad hoc requests and keep a single source of truth

## Goals
1) Provide a weekly (and on-demand) capacity export that answers:
   - Which **shapes** are sellable by **region** (and by tier where applicable)
   - Current **available units** (unallocated), and **planned availability** (forecast in next 2/4/8 weeks)
   - **Lead time** estimates when not immediately available
   - **Headroom policy** summary for each tier (what we assume we must reserve / not sell)
   - **Notes/constraints** that affect quoting (e.g., “H100-8x limited in eu-central; 6–10 week lead time”) 

2) Format must be *Sales-friendly*:
   - single CSV export OR Google Sheet tab with consistent columns
   - human-readable fields (tier names, region names, shape names)
   - includes a “confidence”/“last_updated” indicator

3) Data must align to the Dedicated tier work:
   - uses the canonical tier->shape mapping from Product/Infra
   - matches the same region naming as in quoting tools

Non-goals:
- Not building a full Sales UI; this is an export/report.
- Not changing provisioning logic or admission control.
- Not exposing customer-level utilization or any sensitive internal cost data.

## Proposed output
### Distribution
- Primary: Google Drive shared drive location (owned by Sales Ops), updated weekly.
- Secondary: internal API endpoint for on-demand pull by authorized users.

### Export format (v1)
One row per (region, shape, tier).

Columns:
- report_generated_at (UTC ISO)
- report_window (e.g., “next_8_weeks”)
- region (e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-west)
- tier (Standard | Plus | Premium)
- shape_id (internal stable id)
- shape_name (human name, e.g., “H100-8x”)
- gpu_type (H100 | A100 | L40S)
- gpu_count
- cpu_cores
- ram_gb
- network_gbps (if known)
- sellable_now (yes/no)
- available_units_now (integer)
- max_new_deployments_now (integer; derived from policy)
- forecast_available_units_2w / 4w / 8w (integers; may be blank if unknown)
- estimated_lead_time_weeks (range string, e.g., “0–2”, “6–10”)
- headroom_policy_summary (string, e.g., “Premium: N+1 spare nodes per pool; no overbooking”)
- quota_notes (freeform, short)
- confidence (high/medium/low)
- owner (team alias, e.g., “fleet-ops@redwood”) 

### Guardrails
- Do not include per-customer allocations or contract details.
- Do not include GPU $/hr or margin assumptions (Finance sensitivity).
- Include a “contact_for_exception” field for escalation to Fleet/Deal Desk.

## Data sources (current assumptions)
- Fleet inventory service (authoritative for owned/leased GPU nodes by region + current allocation status)
- Procurement tracker (planned deliveries/returns; used for forecast & lead time ranges)
- Tier->shape mapping (from Product/Infra; should be versioned)
- Capacity model defaults (headroom/overbooking rules by tier)

## Implementation sketch
- Build a small “capacity_exporter” job:
  1) Pull inventory snapshot per region + shape
  2) Apply policy transformations:
     - remove reserved/warm pool inventory from sellable_now calculations
     - enforce headroom assumptions by tier
  3) Join in procurement forecast and collapse into 2/4/8 week buckets
  4) Emit:
     - CSV artifact
     - optional JSON response from internal endpoint

- Add basic validation:
  - if tier->shape mapping missing/unknown, mark confidence=low and add quota_notes
  - if procurement data stale (>14 days), set confidence=low

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CSV export generated successfully in staging and prod with stable columns
- [ ] Export includes at least 3 regions and top shapes used for Dedicated quoting
- [ ] Lead time range populated for non-sellable shapes where procurement data exists
- [ ] Headroom policy summary included and matches approved headroom/overbooking policy
- [ ] Weekly scheduled run (Mon 09:00 PT) + manual trigger documented
- [ ] Access controls documented (who can view in Drive; who can hit API)
- [ ] Sales Ops sign-off that format is usable for quoting

## Open questions
1) Where should the authoritative tier->shape mapping live for programmatic consumption (Confluence is not a source of truth)? If no service exists, we may hardcode a v1 config file with explicit versioning.
2) How should we represent “burst pool” availability (if any) without confusing quoting? Proposal: exclude from sellable_now and add a note pointing to Deal Desk for burst exceptions.
3) Do we need a separate view for “Private/VPC Dedicated” vs standard Dedicated? (assume no for v1; region/shape constraints capture most).
